chunk_findings.detail: The metadata source string acknowledges `shape ASSUMED from the gemini-cli stream-json; the antigravity headless doc names -p and --output-format only`, which means this fixture family is speculative rather than a recorded worker stream matching the task description.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/antigravity/family.json:5

chunk_findings.detail: The rules source points to `ddflow.services.lanes.opencode:STREAM_RULES`, but the manifest and repository files do not contain any module `ddflow.services.lanes.opencode`, which will cause import or attribute lookup errors when `xagent_lab.py` attempts to load the rule source for `opencode-run`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/opencode-run/family.json:10

chunk_findings.detail: `Stream.terminal()` can raise `ValueError: max() arg is an empty sequence` if a stream contains no lines matching any stream rule (for example, a stream that becomes empty or contains only non-matching lines). Given an input stream where `Stream.rule(i)` is `None` for all `i`, line 126 calls `max()` on an empty generator expression, crashing the fault builder and failing test collection or execution.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/xagent_faults.py:126

chunk_findings.detail: `run_pair` invokes `F.build(fam, scenario, tmp, seed)` without `tmp` being defined in the parameter signature or imported in this file (it is only passed as a parameter to `run_pair`), yet `run_pair`'s caller might not supply a valid `tmp` `Path` (it is a required keyword argument without a default). If a caller calls `run_pair(control, fam)` without `tmp=...`, Python raises a `TypeError` due to the missing required keyword-only argument `tmp`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/xagent_lab.py:270

chunk_findings.detail: The fixture declares `"text_mode": "join"`, but its expected event stream still contains the two `agent_message_chunk` outputs as two separate `settled` events with partial text (`"Edited src/a.py; "` and `"tests pass."`). For the `ok.jsonl` stream, a runner that honors `text_mode` should normalize those two chunks into one settled event with text `"Edited src/a.py; tests pass."`, so the expected six-event list will not match the normalized run. If the runner instead ignores `text_mode`, the fixture asserts a join mode that is never exercised, making the fixture’s declared text contract inconsistent with its expected output.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/acp/family.json (`text_mode` / `expect.events`)

chunk_findings.detail: The amp fixture cannot correctly assert the usage contract: the third line of `ok.jsonl` contains both a tool use (`message.content.0.name` exists) and usage (`message.usage.output_tokens` exists), with `input_tokens: 310, output_tokens: 45`, but `expect.events` includes only the fifth line's usage event (`420, 18`) and `expect.usage.tokens` is `438`. Because `usage_mode` is `"delta"`, the two usage objects should either produce two usage events or a total of `730` input / `63` output / `793` tokens. With the rules as written, the `tool` rule shadows the `usage` rule on line 3 under first-match semantics, so the asserted cumulative usage omits 355 tokens; for example, a cap of 350 tokens should already be exceeded after line 3, but the fixture's expected usage remains zero until line 5. Under all-match semantics, the test is also wrong because it is missing the line-3 usage event.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/amp/family.json (`rules` / `expect`)

chunk_findings.detail: The fixture declares `text_mode: "join"` but its `expect.events` still assert two separate `settled` text events for the two assistant delta lines in `ok.jsonl` (`"Edited src/a.py; "` and `"tests pass."`). Given this `ok.jsonl`, if the pair runner honours `text_mode: "join"`, it must normalise those deltas into a single text payload (`"Edited src/a.py; tests pass."`), so the expected-event comparison will fail. If the runner does not honour `text_mode`, then the fixture is asserting unjoined text while claiming join semantics, making the join contract untested.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/gemini/family.json:77

chunk_findings.detail: `_runaway` pops the terminal line from `Stream.lines` but does not update `Stream.objs`, so the object list remains aligned to the old line list. It then calls `s.rewrite("cost", _scale)`, and `Stream.hits` indexes `self.objs` by the new `len(self.lines)`. For an SSE fixture whose terminal event is followed by the normal blank SSE separator, e.g. `data: {"status":"done","cost":1}\n\n`, `terminal()` returns the data line, `pop` removes that line leaving the blank line, but `objs[terminal]` still contains the popped `done`/`cost` object. `rewrite` therefore sees a cost field at that index and writes a rendered copy of the popped terminal object back into the recording. The generated runaway recording still contains the terminal `done` event (with inflated cost) instead of ending without a terminal event, so the runaway/cap scenario is not exercised as intended.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/xagent_faults.py:_runaway

chunk_findings.detail: `derive_status` claims merged-ready only when the worker exited 0, but it only checks `state != "exited"` and never checks `d.exit_code == 0`. Given a normalised stream that ends with a terminal status in `fam.success` while the lane driver reports `st.state == "exited"` and `st.exit_code == 1` (the status object carries the exit code separately, and `run_pair` copies it into `d.exit_code`), the function falls through to `return "merged-ready", ""`. The pair runner then treats a nonzero exit as a successful delegation, and `FakeControl.decide` may accept it.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/xagent_lab.py:251

chunk_findings.detail: `run_acp` sets `d.events = [e.kind for e in res.events]`, i.e. a list of event-kind values, while `Delegation.attributed()` at line 131 expects each event to have `.seq`, `.event`, and `.fields`. Calling `run_acp(...).attributed()` raises `AttributeError` (for example, `'str' object has no attribute 'seq'`), so ACP pairs cannot satisfy the lab's attribution-on-every-event contract and also lose event fields needed for usage, model served, text, and violations.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/xagent_lab.py:446

chunk_findings.detail: `outside` detects writes outside the worktree by a literal `startswith(worktree + "/")` without normalising the path. For `worktree="/work/lane"` and a tool event path `/work/lane/../etc/passwd`, the string check passes, so `outside` returns `[]` even though the resolved path is `/etc/passwd`. Thus `d.violations` remains empty and `derive_status` does not fail for a write outside the worktree.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/xagent_lab.py:232

chunk_findings.detail: The test reads the knob from an ambient `Config()` and then asserts it equals 6. Since the intended knob surface includes configuration files, a project or operator config setting `[lab] fixture_max_age_months = 12` makes `Config().lab.fixture_max_age_months` return 12, so `assert months == 6` fails even though the code correctly honours the configured knob. The later `L.stale(months, ...)` assertions also use that ambient value, so a configured 12 makes the “7 months old: all flagged” assertion fail because 7 is not older than 12. A unit test for the knob’s default behaviour should isolate the default config (or monkeypatch the knob) instead of depending on the developer/CI environment.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_xagent_pair_fakes.py:test_stale_fixtures_are_flagged_by_the_knob_never_failed

chunk_findings.detail: This test only asserts that reported gaps are a subset of the known families: `set(L.gaps()) <= set(FAMILIES)`. It does not assert that unrecorded fixtures are actually reported as gaps. If `L.gaps()` regresses to return `[]` while every `family.json` still has `recorded: false`, the assertion still passes because the empty set is a subset of `FAMILIES`, so the test does not catch the failure it claims to guard.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_xagent_pair_fakes.py:test_unrecorded_fixtures_stay_visible_as_a_gap

chunk_findings.detail: <ddflow-record kind="rule" id="r-task-phase-needs-wave" by="[REDACTED:hostname]-ddflow-7267fe" trust="agent">Every task has a phase, stated dependencies and a wave tag: RULE: every task names the phase whose progress it counts towards, states its dependencies in needs, and carries a wave:N tag (ddflow waves --stamp derives it). A task with no prerequisite carries the tag no-deps, so that none is a decision and not an omission. Work that blocks a phase belongs in that phase; a catch-all such as bugs-2 is only for work no phase serves.</ddflow-record> The added task files and test suite under `tests/fixtures/xagent/` introduce new tasks and code without associating them with a declared phase, state dependencies in `needs`, or carry a `wave:N` / `no-deps` tag, violating rule `r-task-phase-needs-wave`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/gemini/family.json

chunk_findings.detail: The README’s evidence claim is internally inconsistent: line 13 describes each `ok.jsonl`/`ok.sse` as “the recorded stream,” and line 3 says the lab drives “one recorded worker transport,” but line 26 states “Today every fixture is `recorded: false`.” For any fixture in this corpus (for example `tests/fixtures/xagent/claude/ok.jsonl`), the lab is synthetic, yet the README presents it as proof based on recorded transports (“It proves caps, fencing and attribution…”). That misrepresents the test corpus and can cause an operator to treat hand-written fake streams as real recorded evidence.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/README.md:13

chunk_findings.detail: The codex rules match only on `item.type`, not on the enclosing codex event type being `item.completed`. The codex framing clearly uses `item.started` events (`ok.jsonl` line 4 is `{"type":"item.started",...}`), so a valid stream line such as `{"type":"item.started","item":{"id":"x","type":"agent_message","text":"partial"}}` satisfies the rule at lines 36-42 and makes the lab emit a `settled` event before the agent message is complete. Similarly, `{"type":"item.started","item":{"id":"x","type":"file_change","changes":[]}}` satisfies the `file_change` rule at lines 25-32 and emits a `tool` event with a missing/undefined `path`. That breaks the normalised lane contract: partial or not-yet-completed worker items are treated as final lane events.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/codex/family.json:25-43

chunk_findings.detail: The fixture declares `"text_mode": "join"`, but its `expect.events` still contains two separate `settled` text events for the two assistant delta lines in `ok.jsonl`. Given `ok.jsonl` lines 5 and 6 (`"role":"assistant"`, `"delta":true`, text `"Edited src/a.py; "` and `"tests pass."`), a join text mode should normalize these into one settled text event (`"Edited src/a.py; tests pass."`), not two. Therefore the exact-events expectation is inconsistent with the declared mode: if `xagent_lab.py` honors `text_mode: join`, the pair test will fail because it emits one joined event; if it does not honor it, the fixture’s declared text mode is not actually exercised.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/gemini/family.json:text_mode

chunk_findings.detail: `_huge` creates the 300-event stress by duplicating the raw string `s.lines[at]`. It assumes that string is a complete newline-terminated line. If the source recording's selected line is the last line of a JSONL file without a final newline (a valid file), `"".join(s.lines)` in `build` concatenates the original and the 300 copies into one malformed line. For example, `ok.jsonl` containing `{"path":"x"}` with no trailing newline and scenario `huge` produces one line `{"path":"x"}{"path":"x"}...`, so the fake worker emits one event (or invalid JSON), not 300; the `event_buffer=25`/`late=True` drop assertion is not exercised. The code should re-render or add the framing separator.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/xagent_faults.py:184 (`_huge`)

chunk_findings.detail: `_runaway` removes the terminal line before scaling costs and ignores the result of the cost rewrite, so `plan.applies` remains True even when no cost was inflated. If a family's cost is on the terminal event (e.g. `ok.jsonl` has one rule-mapped line `{"type":"result","cost":1}`), `s.terminal()` returns 0, `s.lines.pop(0)` empties the stream, `s.rewrite("cost", _scale)` returns False, and `build` writes an empty recording while returning `applies=True` and `hang=True`. The intended "huge cost" runaway is absent but the matrix believes it applied; the same lies happen for any family with no numeric cost field.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/xagent_faults.py:204 (`_runaway`)

chunk_findings.detail: `derive_status` never checks that `d.exit_code == 0` once `state == "exited"`. A scripted worker that emits a terminal `settled` event with a status in `fam.success` and then exits with code 1 causes `run_pair` to set `st.state == "exited"` and `d.exit_code == 1`; `derive_status` skips the `state != "exited"` branch, sees no error or violation, finds the success terminal, and returns `("merged-ready", "")`. Thus a nonzero exit can be accepted, contradicting the stated exit-code contract and the function’s own docstring.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/xagent_lab.py:derive_status

chunk_findings.detail: `run_acp` returns a `Delegation` that does not satisfy the `Delegation` contract used by the rest of the lab. It sets `d.events = [e.kind for e in res.events]`, so `d.attributed()` raises `AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'seq'` for any ACP run, and it leaves `d.usage` empty and `d.handback` empty even if the recorded `session/update` stream contains usage or text. Given `run_acp(control, load("acp"))`, the intended assertions on normalised lane events, usage basis, and fenced handback cannot pass.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/xagent_lab.py:run_acp

chunk_findings.detail: The wall cap can be delayed indefinitely by a continuous event stream. After the cost enforcer returns, `_bounded` drains events with `while driver.status(h).state == "running" and time.monotonic() < end: list(tee.events(h, idle_s=0.05))`. If a worker emits events faster than the 0.05-second idle timeout, that `list(tee.events(...))` call does not return, so execution never reaches the `driver.interrupt(h)` wall-stop code; the lane is not bounded by `wall_s` until an idle gap occurs.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/xagent_lab.py:_bounded

chunk_findings.detail: The version assertion only checks that a recorded fixture does not literally use the string `"unversioned"`; it does not require a recorded fixture to have a non-empty version. A fixture meta such as `{"recorded": true, "version": "", "source": "fake", "date": "2026-11-14"}` passes because `("" == "unversioned")` is `False` and `not meta["recorded"]` is also `False`, so `False is False`. The test docstring and the harness contract say every fixture records an agent version, so this false pass lets a recorded fixture omit its version.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_xagent_pair_fakes.py:test_each_fixture_says_whether_it_was_recorded

chunk_findings.detail: The metadata source string acknowledges `shape ASSUMED from the gemini-cli stream-json; the antigravity headless doc names -p and --output-format only`, which means this fixture family is speculative rather than a recorded worker stream matching the task description.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/antigravity/family.json:5

chunk_findings.detail: The rules source points to `ddflow.services.lanes.opencode:STREAM_RULES`, but the manifest and repository files do not contain any module `ddflow.services.lanes.opencode`, which will cause import or attribute lookup errors when `xagent_lab.py` attempts to load the rule source for `opencode-run`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/opencode-run/family.json:10

chunk_findings.detail: `Stream.terminal()` can raise `ValueError: max() arg is an empty sequence` if a stream contains no lines matching any stream rule (for example, a stream that becomes empty or contains only non-matching lines). Given an input stream where `Stream.rule(i)` is `None` for all `i`, line 126 calls `max()` on an empty generator expression, crashing the fault builder and failing test collection or execution.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/xagent_faults.py:126

chunk_findings.detail: `run_pair` invokes `F.build(fam, scenario, tmp, seed)` without `tmp` being defined in the parameter signature or imported in this file (it is only passed as a parameter to `run_pair`), yet `run_pair`'s caller might not supply a valid `tmp` `Path` (it is a required keyword argument without a default). If a caller calls `run_pair(control, fam)` without `tmp=...`, Python raises a `TypeError` due to the missing required keyword-only argument `tmp`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/xagent_lab.py:270

chunk_findings.detail: The fixture declares `"text_mode": "join"`, but its expected event stream still contains the two `agent_message_chunk` outputs as two separate `settled` events with partial text (`"Edited src/a.py; "` and `"tests pass."`). For the `ok.jsonl` stream, a runner that honors `text_mode` should normalize those two chunks into one settled event with text `"Edited src/a.py; tests pass."`, so the expected six-event list will not match the normalized run. If the runner instead ignores `text_mode`, the fixture asserts a join mode that is never exercised, making the fixture’s declared text contract inconsistent with its expected output.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/acp/family.json (`text_mode` / `expect.events`)

chunk_findings.detail: The amp fixture cannot correctly assert the usage contract: the third line of `ok.jsonl` contains both a tool use (`message.content.0.name` exists) and usage (`message.usage.output_tokens` exists), with `input_tokens: 310, output_tokens: 45`, but `expect.events` includes only the fifth line's usage event (`420, 18`) and `expect.usage.tokens` is `438`. Because `usage_mode` is `"delta"`, the two usage objects should either produce two usage events or a total of `730` input / `63` output / `793` tokens. With the rules as written, the `tool` rule shadows the `usage` rule on line 3 under first-match semantics, so the asserted cumulative usage omits 355 tokens; for example, a cap of 350 tokens should already be exceeded after line 3, but the fixture's expected usage remains zero until line 5. Under all-match semantics, the test is also wrong because it is missing the line-3 usage event.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/amp/family.json (`rules` / `expect`)

chunk_findings.detail: The fixture declares `text_mode: "join"` but its `expect.events` still assert two separate `settled` text events for the two assistant delta lines in `ok.jsonl` (`"Edited src/a.py; "` and `"tests pass."`). Given this `ok.jsonl`, if the pair runner honours `text_mode: "join"`, it must normalise those deltas into a single text payload (`"Edited src/a.py; tests pass."`), so the expected-event comparison will fail. If the runner does not honour `text_mode`, then the fixture is asserting unjoined text while claiming join semantics, making the join contract untested.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/gemini/family.json:77

chunk_findings.detail: `_runaway` pops the terminal line from `Stream.lines` but does not update `Stream.objs`, so the object list remains aligned to the old line list. It then calls `s.rewrite("cost", _scale)`, and `Stream.hits` indexes `self.objs` by the new `len(self.lines)`. For an SSE fixture whose terminal event is followed by the normal blank SSE separator, e.g. `data: {"status":"done","cost":1}\n\n`, `terminal()` returns the data line, `pop` removes that line leaving the blank line, but `objs[terminal]` still contains the popped `done`/`cost` object. `rewrite` therefore sees a cost field at that index and writes a rendered copy of the popped terminal object back into the recording. The generated runaway recording still contains the terminal `done` event (with inflated cost) instead of ending without a terminal event, so the runaway/cap scenario is not exercised as intended.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/xagent_faults.py:_runaway

chunk_findings.detail: `derive_status` claims merged-ready only when the worker exited 0, but it only checks `state != "exited"` and never checks `d.exit_code == 0`. Given a normalised stream that ends with a terminal status in `fam.success` while the lane driver reports `st.state == "exited"` and `st.exit_code == 1` (the status object carries the exit code separately, and `run_pair` copies it into `d.exit_code`), the function falls through to `return "merged-ready", ""`. The pair runner then treats a nonzero exit as a successful delegation, and `FakeControl.decide` may accept it.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/xagent_lab.py:251

chunk_findings.detail: `run_acp` sets `d.events = [e.kind for e in res.events]`, i.e. a list of event-kind values, while `Delegation.attributed()` at line 131 expects each event to have `.seq`, `.event`, and `.fields`. Calling `run_acp(...).attributed()` raises `AttributeError` (for example, `'str' object has no attribute 'seq'`), so ACP pairs cannot satisfy the lab's attribution-on-every-event contract and also lose event fields needed for usage, model served, text, and violations.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/xagent_lab.py:446

chunk_findings.detail: `outside` detects writes outside the worktree by a literal `startswith(worktree + "/")` without normalising the path. For `worktree="/work/lane"` and a tool event path `/work/lane/../etc/passwd`, the string check passes, so `outside` returns `[]` even though the resolved path is `/etc/passwd`. Thus `d.violations` remains empty and `derive_status` does not fail for a write outside the worktree.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/xagent_lab.py:232

chunk_findings.detail: The test reads the knob from an ambient `Config()` and then asserts it equals 6. Since the intended knob surface includes configuration files, a project or operator config setting `[lab] fixture_max_age_months = 12` makes `Config().lab.fixture_max_age_months` return 12, so `assert months == 6` fails even though the code correctly honours the configured knob. The later `L.stale(months, ...)` assertions also use that ambient value, so a configured 12 makes the “7 months old: all flagged” assertion fail because 7 is not older than 12. A unit test for the knob’s default behaviour should isolate the default config (or monkeypatch the knob) instead of depending on the developer/CI environment.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_xagent_pair_fakes.py:test_stale_fixtures_are_flagged_by_the_knob_never_failed

chunk_findings.detail: This test only asserts that reported gaps are a subset of the known families: `set(L.gaps()) <= set(FAMILIES)`. It does not assert that unrecorded fixtures are actually reported as gaps. If `L.gaps()` regresses to return `[]` while every `family.json` still has `recorded: false`, the assertion still passes because the empty set is a subset of `FAMILIES`, so the test does not catch the failure it claims to guard.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_xagent_pair_fakes.py:test_unrecorded_fixtures_stay_visible_as_a_gap

chunk_findings.detail: `run_pair` invokes `tee = _Tee(driver, plan.event_buffer)` without `plan.event_buffer` existing on `Plan` (or being initialized anywhere in `Plan`'s definition or callers), which raises an `AttributeError: 'Plan' object has no attribute 'event_buffer'` when running any pair test using `run_pair`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/xagent_lab.py:320

chunk_findings.detail: This delta deletes the only `[lab]` configuration section. The deleted file’s own docstring says that a file under `ddflow/config_sections` is what registers a section, and the manifest shows no replacement config section or new knob module. The pair-lab test file is still part of the change, and the previous review round identified `test_stale_fixtures_are_flagged_by_the_knob_never_failed` as reading `Config().lab.fixture_max_age_months`; with `LabConfig` removed and no replacement, `Config()` no longer has a `lab` attribute, so running that test raises `AttributeError`. Even if the test were adjusted, the accepted `[lab].fixture_max_age_months` knob is no longer settable through the ddflow config surface.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/lab.py:1 (deleted)

chunk_findings.detail: `_flood` truncates the stream to `keep = (hits[0][0] if hits else s.first_event()) + 1`, i.e. through the first line that matches a rule. For SSE fixtures such as `opencode-run`, that matching line is a `data: {...}` line and the event is terminated by the following blank line; the slice removes that blank separator. When the plan then adds `--loop`, the fake repeats the truncated raw lines, producing `data: {...}\ndata: {...}\n...` with no blank line between events. Under SSE framing those consecutive `data:` lines are merged into one event (or, if no terminator ever appears, no event is dispatched), so the intended endless stream of tool events is not produced; a flood run on an SSE family will see one malformed/merged event or none instead of repeated events, so the flood/wall-cap contract is not exercised as claimed.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/xagent_faults.py:_flood

chunk_findings.detail: The new bounded `deque` silently discards events that were successfully handed on by the wrapped driver, and `run_pair` later treats the remaining tail as the complete normalised stream. For example, with `plan.event_buffer = 1`, if the driver hands the tee two events — first a `tool` event whose `path` is outside the worktree, then any other event — `_Tee.seen` keeps only the second event. `run_pair` sets `d.events` from that tail, then `finish` computes `d.violations = outside(d.events, worktree)`, so the outside write is missed, and `d.dropped` is still whatever the driver reported (often `0`). `d.write_audit` can therefore be `"paths"` and `derive_status` can miss the violation even though the delegation actually observed an outside write. The same truncation corrupts `usage_summary`, `served_model`, and handback text because those are also computed from `d.events`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/xagent_lab.py:_Tee.__init__

chunk_findings.detail: The new prefix check is wrong when `posixpath.normpath(worktree)` already ends in a separator. For `worktree="/"`, `root` becomes `"//"`, but a path inside that worktree such as `/etc/passwd` normalises to `/etc/passwd` and then `/etc/passwd/`, which does not start with `"//"`. Thus `outside([tool("/etc/passwd")], "/")` reports `/etc/passwd` as outside the worktree even though it is inside `/`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/xagent_lab.py:outside

chunk_findings.detail: The ACP tool normaliser collapses a tool update's `locations` array to only the first entry. Given an ACP session/update event such as `e.kind == "tool"` with `e.data.locations == [{"path": "/work/lane/a.py"}, {"path": "/etc/passwd"}]`, the emitted tool event contains only `/work/lane/a.py`. `finish`/`outside` therefore cannot see the second path, so `d.violations` remains empty and the pair can be reported as fenced/merged-ready even though the worker touched a file outside the worktree. This bypasses the lab's handback-fencing assertion for any recorded ACP tool update carrying more than one location.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/xagent_lab.py:_acp_events (`path = locs[0].get("path", "")`)

chunk_findings.detail: The new ACP parity test checks attribution only through `delegated_by`; it never asserts that each row from `d.attributed()` carries a correct `worked_by`. If a regression in the ACP event builder or `Delegation.attributed()` omits `worked_by` (or sets it to `None`/empty) while preserving `delegated_by`, this test still passes: `all(r["delegated_by"] == control.id ...)` succeeds, and none of the other assertions inspect `worked_by`. That leaves the accepted “attribution (`delegated_by`, `worked_by`) present” contract unguarded for the ACP pair.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_xagent_pair_fakes.py:test_an_acp_pair_carries_the_same_record_as_the_others

chunk_findings.detail: <ddflow-record kind="rule" id="r-task-phase-needs-wave" by="[REDACTED:hostname]-ddflow-7267fe" trust="agent">Every task has a phase, stated dependencies and a wave tag: RULE: every task names the phase whose progress it counts towards, states its dependencies in needs, and carries a wave:N tag (ddflow waves --stamp derives it). A task with no prerequisite carries the tag no-deps, so that none is a decision and not an omission. Work that blocks a phase belongs in that phase; a catch-all such as bugs-2 is only for work no phase serves.</ddflow-record> The added task files and test suite under `tests/fixtures/xagent/` introduce new tasks and code without associating them with a declared phase, state dependencies in `needs`, or carry a `wave:N` / `no-deps` tag, violating rule `r-task-phase-needs-wave`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/gemini/family.json

chunk_findings.detail: The README’s evidence claim is internally inconsistent: line 13 describes each `ok.jsonl`/`ok.sse` as “the recorded stream,” and line 3 says the lab drives “one recorded worker transport,” but line 26 states “Today every fixture is `recorded: false`.” For any fixture in this corpus (for example `tests/fixtures/xagent/claude/ok.jsonl`), the lab is synthetic, yet the README presents it as proof based on recorded transports (“It proves caps, fencing and attribution…”). That misrepresents the test corpus and can cause an operator to treat hand-written fake streams as real recorded evidence.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/README.md:13

chunk_findings.detail: The codex rules match only on `item.type`, not on the enclosing codex event type being `item.completed`. The codex framing clearly uses `item.started` events (`ok.jsonl` line 4 is `{"type":"item.started",...}`), so a valid stream line such as `{"type":"item.started","item":{"id":"x","type":"agent_message","text":"partial"}}` satisfies the rule at lines 36-42 and makes the lab emit a `settled` event before the agent message is complete. Similarly, `{"type":"item.started","item":{"id":"x","type":"file_change","changes":[]}}` satisfies the `file_change` rule at lines 25-32 and emits a `tool` event with a missing/undefined `path`. That breaks the normalised lane contract: partial or not-yet-completed worker items are treated as final lane events.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/codex/family.json:25-43

chunk_findings.detail: The fixture declares `"text_mode": "join"`, but its `expect.events` still contains two separate `settled` text events for the two assistant delta lines in `ok.jsonl`. Given `ok.jsonl` lines 5 and 6 (`"role":"assistant"`, `"delta":true`, text `"Edited src/a.py; "` and `"tests pass."`), a join text mode should normalize these into one settled text event (`"Edited src/a.py; tests pass."`), not two. Therefore the exact-events expectation is inconsistent with the declared mode: if `xagent_lab.py` honors `text_mode: join`, the pair test will fail because it emits one joined event; if it does not honor it, the fixture’s declared text mode is not actually exercised.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/gemini/family.json:text_mode

chunk_findings.detail: `_huge` creates the 300-event stress by duplicating the raw string `s.lines[at]`. It assumes that string is a complete newline-terminated line. If the source recording's selected line is the last line of a JSONL file without a final newline (a valid file), `"".join(s.lines)` in `build` concatenates the original and the 300 copies into one malformed line. For example, `ok.jsonl` containing `{"path":"x"}` with no trailing newline and scenario `huge` produces one line `{"path":"x"}{"path":"x"}...`, so the fake worker emits one event (or invalid JSON), not 300; the `event_buffer=25`/`late=True` drop assertion is not exercised. The code should re-render or add the framing separator.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/xagent_faults.py:184 (`_huge`)

chunk_findings.detail: `_runaway` removes the terminal line before scaling costs and ignores the result of the cost rewrite, so `plan.applies` remains True even when no cost was inflated. If a family's cost is on the terminal event (e.g. `ok.jsonl` has one rule-mapped line `{"type":"result","cost":1}`), `s.terminal()` returns 0, `s.lines.pop(0)` empties the stream, `s.rewrite("cost", _scale)` returns False, and `build` writes an empty recording while returning `applies=True` and `hang=True`. The intended "huge cost" runaway is absent but the matrix believes it applied; the same lies happen for any family with no numeric cost field.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/xagent_faults.py:204 (`_runaway`)

chunk_findings.detail: `derive_status` never checks that `d.exit_code == 0` once `state == "exited"`. A scripted worker that emits a terminal `settled` event with a status in `fam.success` and then exits with code 1 causes `run_pair` to set `st.state == "exited"` and `d.exit_code == 1`; `derive_status` skips the `state != "exited"` branch, sees no error or violation, finds the success terminal, and returns `("merged-ready", "")`. Thus a nonzero exit can be accepted, contradicting the stated exit-code contract and the function’s own docstring.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/xagent_lab.py:derive_status

chunk_findings.detail: `run_acp` returns a `Delegation` that does not satisfy the `Delegation` contract used by the rest of the lab. It sets `d.events = [e.kind for e in res.events]`, so `d.attributed()` raises `AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'seq'` for any ACP run, and it leaves `d.usage` empty and `d.handback` empty even if the recorded `session/update` stream contains usage or text. Given `run_acp(control, load("acp"))`, the intended assertions on normalised lane events, usage basis, and fenced handback cannot pass.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/xagent_lab.py:run_acp

chunk_findings.detail: The wall cap can be delayed indefinitely by a continuous event stream. After the cost enforcer returns, `_bounded` drains events with `while driver.status(h).state == "running" and time.monotonic() < end: list(tee.events(h, idle_s=0.05))`. If a worker emits events faster than the 0.05-second idle timeout, that `list(tee.events(...))` call does not return, so execution never reaches the `driver.interrupt(h)` wall-stop code; the lane is not bounded by `wall_s` until an idle gap occurs.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/xagent_lab.py:_bounded

chunk_findings.detail: The version assertion only checks that a recorded fixture does not literally use the string `"unversioned"`; it does not require a recorded fixture to have a non-empty version. A fixture meta such as `{"recorded": true, "version": "", "source": "fake", "date": "2026-11-14"}` passes because `("" == "unversioned")` is `False` and `not meta["recorded"]` is also `False`, so `False is False`. The test docstring and the harness contract say every fixture records an agent version, so this false pass lets a recorded fixture omit its version.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_xagent_pair_fakes.py:test_each_fixture_says_whether_it_was_recorded

chunk_findings.detail: `--loop` repeats the last written `line` verbatim without ensuring it is newline-terminated. If the recording’s final line lacks a trailing newline, the loop emits an unbounded, unterminated concatenation rather than a stream of lines. For example, with `printf '{"type":"result","status":"ok"}' rec.jsonl` and `python fake_agent.py rec.jsonl --loop`, stdout becomes `{"type":"result","status":"ok"}{"type":"result","status":"ok"}...` as a single line. A line-oriented lane reader will not see the first event, so the intended firehose/wall-cap scenario can hang or fail instead of producing repeated events.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/lane_driver/fake_agent.py:62-65 (`--loop`)

chunk_findings.detail:
The change deletes the only `[lab]` config-section declaration while the stated acceptance requires `fixture_max_age_months` to be settable via file/CLI/MCP. The removed file’s own contract is that a file in `ddflow/config_sections` registers its section; with `ddflow/config_sections/lab.py` gone and no replacement in the manifest, a config file such as:

```toml
[lab]
fixture_max_age_months = 6
```

is no longer recognized as a declared `lab` section, and `ddflow config` cannot expose the knob. That removes required lab configuration surface.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/lab.py:1

chunk_findings.detail: The new `flood` scenario makes the worker stream endless (`plan.extra.append("--loop")`) but then sets `plan.hang = False`. That marks the run as a normal terminating run even though the recording has been truncated to a single non-terminal tool line and the `--loop` flag is intended to keep emitting it “without end”. For example, running scenario `flood` against the codex fixture produces a stream with no terminal event and a fake agent that never exits; the pair runner, following `plan.hang`, treats it as an ordinary finished run rather than a hanging/wall-capped run, so the test either blocks waiting for termination or receives an unexpected wall-cap exit instead of exercising the intended wall-cap path. The other no-terminal fault builders (`_runaway`, `_cancel`) set `plan.hang = True`, so this line contradicts the scenario contract.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/xagent_faults.py:_flood

chunk_findings.detail: The new bounded `deque` makes `_Tee` silently discard the oldest events once `plan.event_buffer` events have been seen, but the delegation still takes `d.dropped` from `st.dropped`, which is the underlying driver's drop count, not the tee's eviction count. A worker can emit more than `plan.event_buffer` events while the consumer keeps up, so `st.dropped` remains `0` even though `_Tee.seen` has evicted early events. For example, with `plan.event_buffer=1`, a stream whose first event is a hidden `model_served` event or a `tool` write outside the worktree, followed by innocuous events, leaves only the last event in `d.events`; `outside()` misses the write, `write_audit` is reported as `"paths"` because `d.dropped == 0`, and `served_model` cannot flag the hidden model. The lab can therefore certify a clean pair from an incomplete recording.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/xagent_lab.py:_Tee.__init__

chunk_findings.detail: For `worktree="/"`, `posixpath.normpath(worktree)` returns `"/"`, and the new code turns it into root `"//"`. A tool event path such as `/etc/passwd` normalizes to `/etc/passwd/`, which does not start with `"//"`, so it is reported as a write outside the worktree even though every absolute path is inside the root worktree. The root case is mishandled because a slash is appended to an already-root normalized path.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/xagent_lab.py:outside

chunk_findings.detail: The refactor moves status derivation into `finish`, but ACP permission results are still only available from `res.permissions` and are not passed to `finish` or normalised into lane events by `_acp_events`. After `finish` has already chosen `d.status` from the terminal stop reason, the new code changes only `d.reason` when a permission was unanswered. Thus, for an ACP fixture whose `res.stop_reason` is in `fam.success` and whose `res.permissions` contains an unanswered entry such as `("approve", False)`, the delegation can be left with `d.status == "merged-ready"` while `d.reason` says the permission was unanswered. The previous code explicitly set `d.status = "needs-input"` for that case, so this change loses the approval gate and can report an unapproved ACP run as accepted.
chunk_findings.title: tests/fixtures/xagent/xagent_lab.py:run_acp

chunk_findings.detail: The accepted knob is `[lab].fixture_max_age_months`, but this changed test now reads `Config().hooks.fixture_max_age_months`. The same change deletes `ddflow/config_sections/lab.py` and the `[lab]` knob upgrade template, so this test no longer exercises the documented lab knob at all. For example, a tree configured with the accepted `[lab] fixture_max_age_months = 6` and no `[hooks] fixture_max_age_months` will make this test fail (or pass while testing an unrelated hooks default), so the stale-fixture contract is not actually being checked as specified.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_xagent_pair_fakes.py:test_stale_fixtures_are_flagged_by_the_knob_never_failed

chunk_findings.detail: The new recorded-version guard still permits non-version placeholders: a fixture meta such as `{"recorded": true, "version": null, "source": "rec", "date": "2026-11-14"}` passes because `None not in ("", "unversioned")` is true; `False` and `0` pass too. This is the previous finding #10 not fully answered: the test claims a recorded fixture “names the agent's version,” but a null/false/zero value is not a named version, so invalid recorded fixtures can still pass.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_xagent_pair_fakes.py:test_each_fixture_says_whether_it_was_recorded
